newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols drop after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols drop after FOMC.

text.p: Implied volatility for July U.S. Treasury bond options nosedived, as expected, after news the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at today's policymaking meeting.
July volatility plunged to 7.94 percent immediately after the Fed announcement at 1415 EDT and kept falling to finish the session at 7.75 percent.
"Volatility measures anticipation, and once the information is out, there is no more anticipation and volatility declines," said an analyst for a brokerage firm on the CBOT floor.

What was surprising, he noted, is that volatility had begun to drift lower even before the Fed made its decision known. Around midday, July volatility had edged down to 8.40 percent from the day's high of 8.69 percent established on the opening.

"Volatility, which should have been increasing, actually began to decrease before the announcement came out," said the brokerage analyst. "What that tells you is that the locals in the pit felt there would be no change in policy."

After the Fed announcement, June Treasury bond futures quickly rallied to the day's high of 110-12, then pulled back just as fast to trade moderately lower before edging back up into the close. The contract settled down 2/32 at 109-27.
September bond volatility ended at 8.14 percent, down from 8.50 percent at the opening.

The Federal Open Market Committee left the federal funds rate, which commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans, at 5.50 percent and the discount rate the Fed charges the banks at 5.0 percent.
Earlier in the session, several trading firms established positions in bond options designed to profit from a strong directional move in the underlying futures that never materialized, traders said.

One firm bought 3,000 July 108-00 puts at premiums between 36/64 and 39/64. By the close, the puts were valued at 30/64. Another trade involved the purchase of 2,500 July 112-00 calls at 17/64. The calls were said to be worth 12/64 at the close after both volatility and the futures price moved lower.
Traders said volatilities could remain subdued with June futures still trapped between 109-16 and 110-16.
But volatilities should start to climb again next week, some traders predicted, as fresh economic data revive the debate over the Fed's next move.

Eurodollar volatility levels declined across the board as futures pushed higher, revisiting "comfortable" levels after the Fed news, a CME broker said. September fell 0.5 point to 9.4 percent and December shed 0.65 point to 10.8 percent.
December Eurodollar futures ended six basis points higher at 93.735.
